197 FERC ¶ 61,023
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

Before Commissioners:  Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                                        David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                                        Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.


ORDER ACCEPTING 2027 BUSINESS PLANS AND BUDGETS

(Issued October 15, 2026)

On August 25, 2026, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) filed the 2027 business plans and budgets for NERC, each Regional Entity, and the Western Interconnection Regional Advisory Body (WIRAB) (collectively, 2027 NERC Application).  For the reasons discussed below, we accept the 2027 NERC Application, as well as the associated attachments and updates, and authorize issuance of billing invoices to fund the fiscal year 2027 operations of NERC, the Regional Entities, and WIRAB.
Background
Regulatory History
Section 215 of the Federal Power Act (FPA) provides that the Commission may certify an Electric Reliability Organization (ERO), the purpose of which is to develop mandatory and enforceable Reliability Standards, subject to Commission review and approval.  Reliability Standards may be enforced by the ERO, subject to Commission oversight, or by the Commission independently.  Pursuant to section 215 of the FPA, the Commission established a process to select and certify an ERO, and subsequently certified NERC.
Section 215(c)(2)(B) of the FPA provides that the ERO must have rules that “allocate equitably reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among end users for all activities under this section.”  In Order No. 672, the Commission implemented the requirements of section 215 of the FPA, which generally provides for Commission authorization of funding for “statutory” functions conducted by the ERO and the Regional Entities (i.e., those functions carried out pursuant to section 215 of the FPA).  Among other things, Order No. 672 established requirements for funding the ERO and approval of an ERO business plan and budget.  Moreover, the Commission’s regulations require the ERO to file with the Commission the ERO’s proposed annual budget for statutory and non-statutory activities 130 days before the beginning of the ERO’s fiscal year.  The ERO’s filing must contain the annual budgets of the ERO and each Regional Entity for statutory and non-statutory activities and provide supporting materials, including the ERO’s and each Regional Entity’s complete business plan and organizational chart.  The filing must also explain the proposed collection of all dues, fees, and charges, as well as the proposed expenditure of funds collected.
In July 2006, the Commission approved the establishment of a regional advisory body for the Western Interconnection, WIRAB, and granted the request that WIRAB receive funding for the reasonable costs of its FPA section 215(j) activities.  Further, the Commission directed WIRAB to develop a budget and related information for review through the ERO budget approval process.
2027 NERC Application
The 2027 NERC Application contains the proposed business plans and budgets of NERC, each of the six Regional Entities, and WIRAB for the year ending December 31, 2027.  NERC states that it prepared its 2027 business plan and budget and worked with the Regional Entities in developing their business plans and budgets through a rigorous process providing opportunity for review and input by the NERC Board of Trustees Finance and Audit Committee and stakeholders.  
NERC states that the proposed assessment for the NERC, Regional Entities, and WIRAB budgets for 2027 allocable to the United States is $285,049,851, an increase of $24,078,516 (9.23%) over the $260,971,335 overall 2026 budget allocable to the United States.  This amount includes $112,790,742 for NERC funding, $171,655,944 for Regional Entity funding, and $603,165 for WIRAB funding.  NERC explains that it will continue to allocate costs to end users in the United States based on net energy for load.  NERC maintains that its proposed total United States net funding requirement for NERC, the Regional Entities, and WIRAB is equivalent to $0.0000664 per end-user                    kilowatt-hour (kWh), based on the aggregate net energy for load of the United States in 2025. 
In addition to the NERC, Regional Entity, and WIRAB business plans and budgets (2027 NERC Application Attachments 2-9), the 2027 NERC Application contains various attachments including:  Summary Tables for NERC and Regional Entity Proposed 2027 Budgets and Assessments (Attachment 1); NERC Management’s Responses to Stakeholder Comments Submitted on Posted Draft of NERC’s 2027 Business Plan and Budget (Attachment 10); Calculations of Adjustments to the Alberta Electric System Operator, Ontario Independent Electric System Operator, New Brunswick, and Québec 2027 NERC Assessments (Attachment 11); NERC Board of Trustee Proposed Compensation Changes (Attachment 12); Summary of NERC Review of and Participation in Development of Regional Entity 2027 Business Plans and Budgets (Attachment 13); Metrics Comparing Regional Entity Operations Based on the 2027 Budgets (Attachment 14); and Metrics on NERC and Regional Entity Administrative (Indirect) Costs Based on the 2026 and 2027 Budgets (Attachment 15).
Notice and Responsive Pleading
Notice of NERC’s August 25, 2026 filing was published in the Federal Register, 91 Fed. Reg. 55563 (Aug. 28, 2026), with interventions and protests due on or before September 15, 2026.  None was filed.  
Discussion
NERC Business Plan and Budget
Proposal
NERC states that its 2027 business plan and budget is organized based on the following program areas:  (1) Reliability Standards; (2) Compliance Assurance, Organization Registration and Certification, and Compliance Enforcement; (3) Reliability Assessments, Performance Analysis, Data Analytics, Engineering, and Power Risk Issues and Strategic Management (PRISM); (4) Situation Awareness; (5) Event Analysis; (6) Electricity Information Sharing and Analysis Center (E-ISAC), including the Cyber Risk Information Sharing Program (CRISP); (7) Personnel Certification and Credential Maintenance; and (8) Training and Education.  NERC explains that these statutory, or “direct,” program areas are supported by its Corporate Services, or “indirect,” programs:  (1) General and Administrative; (2) Legal and Regulatory; (3) Business Technology; (4) Human Resources and Operations; and (5) Finance and Accounting.  For the statutory program areas, NERC describes each program, identifies the program’s goals and objectives, and provides the Commission-accepted number of full-time equivalent employees (FTE), as well as the FTEs budgeted for 2027.  NERC also provides 2026 accepted budget data for comparison to the 2027 proposed budget data. 
NERC’s proposed total funding requirement for 2027, encompassing U.S. and Canadian activities, is $140,316,090, which is an increase of $11,609,523 (9.02%) over NERC’s 2026 total funding requirement of $128,706,567.  NERC’s proposed 2027 net funding requirement from assessments is $125,055,568 (i.e., the total funding requirement less $15,260,522 in funding from other sources), of which $112,790,742 is allocated to the United States, an increase of $11,306,140 (9.94%) over the 2026 net funding requirement from assessments of $113,749,428.  
NERC’s proposed 2027 budget, excluding E-ISAC costs of $48,961,009, is $91,082,991, an increase of $7,920,496 (9.52%) over its 2026 budget less E-ISAC costs of $83,162,494.  NERC states that the 2027 budget increase is attributable to, in part, additional personnel expenses (additional FTEs and increases to salary and benefits), additional meetings and travel expenses (increase in in-person stakeholder engagement and travel cost increases), and additional operating expenses (increased contracts and consultants expenses and office costs).  
According to NERC, the 2027 budget of $48,961,009 for E-ISAC, including funding for CRISP, reflects an increase of $3,779,258 (8.36%) over its 2026 budget of $45,181,751.  NERC explains that the E-ISAC budget increase reflects, in part, additional contractor and consultant costs and that the increase of 2.35 FTEs reflects the addition of positions to support unified coordination initiatives, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning models, and vendor affiliate program support.
NERC states that the proposed 2027 business plan and budget reflects a provision for working capital and operating reserve funding in the amount of $18,036,962, which is a decrease of $2,871,117 (13.73%) from the 2026 funding level of $20,908,079.  NERC proposes a 2027 staffing level of 288.19 FTEs, an increase of 15.59 FTEs (5.72%) from the 2026 budget staffing level of 272.60 FTEs.
NERC states that it did not collect any penalties in the period between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026, and requests an exception to section 1107.2 of the NERC Rules of Procedure to permit it to use $456,000 from the NERC Assessment Stabilization Reserve to reduce the 2027 assessments.
Commission Determination
We accept NERC’s 2027 business plan and budget.  We find that NERC’s 2027 budget is reasonable and that the associated costs of NERC’s jurisdictional functions are allocated equitably among end users in the United States.  Additionally, based on the details provided by NERC in its application, we grant NERC’s request for an exception under section 1107 of the NERC Rules of Procedure and approve the withdrawal of $456,000 from the NERC Assessment Stabilization Reserve.  We note that the decision here is limited to this case.  The Commission will address any future requests for an exception to section 1107.2 of the NERC Rules of Procedure based on the facts at that time.
Regional Entity Business Plans and Budgets
Proposal
The 2027 NERC Application includes the 2027 business plans and budgets of each Regional Entity.  The proposed total assessment for the Regional Entities that is allocable to the United States is $171,655,944, which represents a $13,920,654 (8.83%) increase from the 2026 budgeted level of $157,735,290.  NERC states that it reviewed the Regional Entity business plans and budgets and concludes that each Regional Entity proposes necessary and adequate resources to carry out its delegated functions.  
NERC requests, pursuant to section 1107.4 of the NERC Rules of Procedure, an exception to section 1107.2 of the NERC Rules of Procedure to:  (1) permit MRO, NPCC, ReliabilityFirst, SERC, and Texas RE to deposit penalty monies received during the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, into their assessment stabilization reserves; and (2) allow MRO, NPCC, ReliabilityFirst, SERC, and Texas RE to use penalties collected prior to July 1, 2025 and held in their respective assessment stabilization reserves to reduce 2027 assessments.  NERC states that NPCC proposes to place $42,823 in penalties collected during the 12 months ending June 30, 2026 into the NPCC Assessment Stabilization Reserve and use $300,000 from the NPCC Assessment Stabilization Reserve to offset NPCC’s 2027 assessments.  NERC states that ReliabilityFirst proposes to use $780,477 of penalty funds collected during the 12 months ending June 30, 2026 to offset ReliabilityFirst’s 2027 assessments.  NERC states that SERC proposes to place $2,649,700 of penalties collected between July 1, 2025 and            June 30, 2026 into the SERC Assessment Stabilization Reserve and to release $1,983,755 from the SERC Assessment Stabilization Reserve to offset SERC’s 2027 assessments.  NERC states that Texas RE proposes to use $385,000 of penalties collected between              July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026 and to release $1,750,000 from the Texas RE Assessment Stabilization Reserve to offset Texas RE’s 2027 assessments.  Further, MRO states that it proposes to use $100,000 of penalty funds collected during the 12 months ending             June 30, 2026, plus $14,939 of earned interest, and to release $1,129,846 from the MRO Assessment Stabilization Reserve to offset MRO’s 2027 assessments.  
For 2027, NERC states that WECC proposes to use $1,145,000 of Peak Donation Reserves to fund a gas-electric interface study, AI projects, and data management projects.  NERC states that WECC anticipates spending the remaining $1,370,000 in its Peak Donation Reserves between 2026 and 2027.  
Commission Determination
We find that each Regional Entity submission reasonably supports the level of expenditures identified in their respective budgets and that each Regional Entity is focused on adequately staffing and funding all of their respective program areas to perform the delegated statutory functions.  Accordingly, we accept the Regional Entity business plans and budgets.  Additionally, based on the details provided by NERC in its application, we grant NERC’s request to allow for an exception under section 1107 of the NERC Rules of Procedure and permit MRO, NPCC, ReliabilityFirst, SERC, and Texas RE to deposit the penalty monies received for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026 into their assessment stabilization reserves, as well as to allow MRO, NPCC, ReliabilityFirst, SERC, and Texas RE to use penalties collected prior to July 1, 2025 and held in their respective assessment stabilization reserves to reduce 2027 assessments.  The Commission will address any future requests for an exception to section 1107.2 of the NERC Rules of Procedure based on the facts at that time.  
WIRAB Business Plan and Budget
Proposal
WIRAB proposes statutory expenses of $882,845 in 2027, a $20,365 (2.36%) increase from its 2026 budget of $862,480.  To fund its operations in 2027, WIRAB proposes a statutory assessment of $709,845, an increase of $3,765 (0.53%) from the 2026 assessment of $706,080.  The proposed statutory assessment includes $603,165 allocable to end users in the United States, an increase of $1,543 (0.26%) from the 2026 amount of $601,622.  WIRAB’s budget for FTEs in 2027 is 3.00 FTEs, which is the same as the 2026 budgeted level of FTEs.
The 2027 NERC Application indicates that WIRAB will pursue the following four strategic initiatives in 2027:  (1) advise WECC on interdependencies between the natural gas and electric systems and the implications for the reliable operation of the Western Interconnection; (2) advise WECC and states to address the reliability risks of resource procurement competition associated with behind-the-meter and co-located resources at large load facilities; (3) advise WECC to incorporate extreme weather and climate-driven scenarios into reliability assessments and long-term planning processes; and (4) advise WECC and states to close the reliability gap on large load emergency operations and demand response in the Western Interconnection.  
Commission Determination
Based on the information provided in the instant filing, we conclude that WIRAB’s 2027 business plan and budget is reasonable and, accordingly, accept it.
The Commission orders:
(A) NERC’s 2027 business plan and budget is hereby accepted.  
(B) The Regional Entities’ 2027 business plans and budgets are hereby accepted.
(C) NERC’s request for waiver of section 1107.2 of its Rules of Procedure for NERC, MRO, NPCC, ReliabilityFirst, SERC, and Texas RE is hereby granted.
(D) NERC’s request for WECC’s use of the Peak Reliability Donation Reserve account funds is hereby granted.
(E) WIRAB’s 2027 business plan and budget is hereby accepted. 
By the Commission.  
( S E A L )


Debbie-Anne A. Reese,
Secretary.
